title: Answer the requests the authorizer can't take

blocks.text: A terminal vendor shipped a software update with a bug: now and then its terminals send a purchase or an authorization without an amount. The authorizer behind the server can't decide on those, and today the terminals wait out their 30 seconds, then reverse something the server never processed. The scheme's rules say such a request gets response code `30` (format error), at once.

`RequiredFields` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/RequiredFields.java` is the first participant of the server's chain, ahead of the authorizer and `SendResponse`. Its `prepare` already works. Finish the two methods marked `TODO`:

items: `isComplete(...)`: which requests the authorizer can take;
`refuse(...)`: how the transaction of any other request ends.

blocks.text: When you're done, a request without an amount gets its `30` from `SendResponse` and never reaches the authorizer, its terminal recognises the answer as its own, and every other request, the terminals' echoes included, goes on as before. About ten lines in total.
The tests deploy a real TransactionManager with Q2, in the test's own JVM, and feed it requests the way `IncomingListener` does.

cases.says: a purchase with an amount goes on to the authorizer and the terminal gets its approval
an authorization with an amount goes on to the authorizer and the terminal gets its approval
a refused request still gets its response, because the response is in the Context before the participant votes ABORTED
the refusal is built from the request, so it carries the STAN and terminal ID the terminal matches it by
a network message carries no amount and is not refused for it
the response is a copy, so the request in the Context keeps its MTI and gets no response code

origin.section: 1.4 A Participant Decides in `prepare`, and an Abort Still Answers

concepts: A participant decides in prepare and puts a response built from the request into the Context before it votes, so SendResponse answers on the abort path too.
